page: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance in the DDSv5 family, built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with hyperthreading on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. Memory allocation stands at 256 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capacity includes 2,458 GB of directly attached local SSD storage. The CPU cache architecture provides 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA extensions for acceleration.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64ds_v5 shows strong multi-core computing capabilities alongside average single-core performance. Multi-threaded CPU tests, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, place the instance in the upper quartile of performance. Large-block memory bandwidth tests indicate strong read and write throughput for uncached data blocks, reaching 291.37 GB/sec and 132.39 GB/sec respectively. Operational benchmarks reflect high performance in static web serving at 52.02 GB/sec and Redis SET operations exceeding 62 million operations per second. However, single-core benchmarks, such as single-threaded gzip compression and single-core stress-ng tests, perform within the average middle tier.

From an architecture and workload fit perspective, the inclusion of 2,458 GB of local SSD storage alongside 64 dedicated vCPUs eliminates the need for auxiliary local drives in disk-intensive scenarios. The system demonstrates a clear tradeoff between massive multi-core throughput and moderate single-threaded latency. While large language model inference for 70B parameter models shows lower text generation speeds, prompt processing for smaller models remains performant. Consequently, the D64ds_v5 is well suited for enterprise database operations, software build servers, web application clusters, and data processing pipelines that leverage high thread concurrency and local storage access.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, 256 GB of system memory, and 2,458 GB of fast local SSD storage. Designed with a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, it delivers strong multi-core processing performance alongside elevated uncached memory bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high efficiency across parallel computing tasks, software compilation, extended instruction execution, and high-throughput Redis or database operations. While single-core performance and large language model text generation remain in the average to lower categories, its substantial thread count and local storage provisioning make it a cost-effective solution for resource-intensive workloads. The instance exhibits balanced performance for multi-threaded enterprise applications, static web serving, relational database hosting, and batch processing environments.
